ruleName: Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions (Including Immovable Obstructions)
imagePrompt: Show a modern, semi-realistic illustration (75% realistic, 25% stylised) in junior golf quiz style. A golfer stands just off the putting green with a putter, preparing a shot. The golf ball rests just off the edge of a neatly trimmed green, with a sprinkler head clearly visible between the ball and the flagstick in the background, directly on the line of play. The player's intended stance and swing are not affected by the sprinkler head. The scene should clearly depict the layout but must not include any text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer with a putter stands just off the edge of a putting green preparing to play, with a golf ball close to the green fringe. A sprinkler head is directly between the ball and the hole, but does not interfere with the golfer's lie, stance or swing.

sceneSpec.setting: Edge of a putting green on a well-kept golf course, with short grass on the green and slightly longer grass just off it.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer preparing to putt from just off the green, holding a putter and focusing on the situation.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Golf ball resting just off the putting green, a short distance from the fringe.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The golfer is evaluating how to play the shot with the sprinkler head directly in the line between the ball and the hole, but not interfering with the player's stance or swing.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Clarifies relief is not given when an immovable obstruction is only on the line of play and does not interfere with lie, stance or area of intended swing.
mustShow: A golf ball just off the green
A sprinkler head between the ball and the hole
The golfer preparing to putt, with normal stance and swing unobstructed
mustNotShow: Any text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles

questions.title: Sprinkler Head Between Ball and Hole, Not Touching You or Your Swing
questions.question: Your ball is just next to the green, and you want to putt. There is a sprinkler head in your way between your ball and the hole, but it does not touch your ball, feet or club when you swing. What should you do?

choices.text: You get to move the ball for free because the sprinkler head is in the way of your shot.
You get to move the ball for free because you are using your putter.
You don't get to move the ball because the sprinkler head does not touch your ball, feet or the club when you swing.
You can move the sprinkler head before you hit your shot.

questions.explanation: You cannot move your ball for free if the sprinkler head only sits between your ball and the hole and does not touch your ball, feet or club when you swing. (Rule 16.1a)

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A round metal cap in the ground that sprays water to help the grass grow.
The way you stand when you get ready to hit the golf ball.
When you are allowed to move your ball to a better spot without penalty.

questions.teachingTip: Show kids a sprinkler head on the course and help them practise where free relief is allowed and where it isn't.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids might think they can always move the ball when something is in their way.
Some may believe using a putter changes the rule.
A student might think it's ok to move or pick up the sprinkler head.

questions.title: Sprinkler Head on Line of Play Off the Putting Green
questions.question: Your ball lies just off the putting green and you wish to putt towards the hole. A sprinkler head is directly on your line of play between your ball and the hole, but it does not interfere with your lie, stance or area of intended swing. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: You are entitled to free relief because the sprinkler head is on your line of play.
You are entitled to free relief because you are using a putter.
You are not entitled to free relief because the sprinkler head does not interfere with your lie, stance or area of intended swing.
You may move the sprinkler head before playing.

questions.explanation: You are not entitled to free relief when an immovable obstruction, such as a sprinkler head, is only on your line of play but does not interfere with your lie, stance or area of intended swing. (Rule 16.1a)
